issues.legal_issue: A High Court may not dismiss an appeal for lack of standing on the ground that an amendment alleging hereditary office was impermissible when the amendment was allowed, its costs were accepted, and the opposing party conceded hereditary status before the Tribunal.
material_facts: The petitioner brought a proceeding under Sections 8 and 10 of the Sikh Gurdwara Act, 1925, concerning whether an institution was a Sikh Gurdwara.
After a standing objection was raised, the Tribunal allowed an amendment alleging that the petitioner was a hereditary office-holder, subject to costs.
The opposing party accepted the costs and later conceded before the Tribunal that the petitioner was a hereditary office-holder.
The Tribunal decided the preliminary standing issue in the petitioner’s favour and later ruled on the merits.
The High Court dismissed the appeal for lack of standing, holding that the amendment should not have been allowed.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s order and remanded the appeal for a decision on the merits of whether the institution was a Sikh Gurdwara.
issues.legal_principle: In a petition under Sections 8 and 10 of the Sikh Gurdwara Act, 1925, the High Court was not justified in rejecting standing solely because the Tribunal had allowed an amendment alleging hereditary office where the opposing party accepted the costs imposed for that amendment and conceded hereditary status before the Tribunal. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: appeal_from_dismissal_of_institution_status_petition and amendment_to_allege_hereditary_office_allowed and opponent_accepted_amendment_costs and opponent_conceded_hereditary_office and tribunal_decided_standing_for_petitioner

predicates.appeal_from_dismissal_of_institution_sta: A party appealed after a court dismissed a petition concerning the status of a religious institution.
predicates.amendment_to_allege_hereditary_office_al: The tribunal allowed the petitioner to amend the petition to allege hereditary office.
predicates.opponent_accepted_amendment_costs: The opposing party accepted the costs imposed for allowing the amendment.
predicates.opponent_conceded_hereditary_office: The opposing party conceded before the tribunal that the petitioner held hereditary office.
predicates.tribunal_decided_standing_for_petitioner: The tribunal decided the preliminary issue of the petitioner’s standing in the petitioner’s favour.

issues.definition: When an appeal from dismissal of an institution-status petition follows an allowed amendment alleging hereditary office, acceptance of its costs, the opponent’s concession of hereditary office, and a tribunal decision for the petitioner on standing, the appeal is allowed and the case is remanded for a merits decision.
